_README: MEASURED solver family per shipped family -- what actually cracked it, not what
the builder declared. This is the honest label for what a question IS.
A family here is NOT a defect. The eval is tools-free, and every one of these held
against a multi-vendor oracle pool with no tools at its shipping preset. What these
numbers say is: (a) how cheap the MECHANICAL route is, which is aging risk -- a
family a library cracks in 0.001s on a tiny instance will fall first as models get
better at simulating solvers in-head; and (b) which SKILL the question exercises,
which is the diversity metric that matters.
self-declared NATIVE['core'] and this field disagree often, and this one wins:
2411.04916 declares itself geometric (kissing numbers in 17-21 dimensions) and is
seconds = median over 8 seeds at the shipping preset, graded by the module's own

families.constraint_search: propagation + backtracking: SAT/CDCL, CSP/GAC, exact cover/DLX, graph colouring
families.subset_sum_knapsack: meet-in-the-middle, dynamic programming over sums, lattice/integer-relation
families.brute_force_structure: exhaustive or near-exhaustive search over a small structured space
families.paper_constructive: the paper's own constructive procedure, implemented directly

2110.05917.attack: CDCL SAT on the shipped CNF

2506.23363.attack: gadget recovery then CDCL on decoded 3-SAT

2302.11250.attack: Algorithm X exact cover with MRV

not_yet_attacked: Every shipped family NOT listed above has never had a domain-standard attack run
against it. Absence from `measured` is absence of evidence, not evidence of
hardness. 23 of 23 families attacked so far have a cheap mechanical route.
